hints: Focus on the two axes separately, melting point depends on structure and bonding while first ionisation energy depends on atomic structure.
Recall that Si has giant covalent bonding so a very high melting point, while P is simple molecular so very low, with Al just above Mg.
Remember the dip from Mg to Al in ionisation energy because Al loses a higher energy 3p electron, giving the left to right order Al, Mg, Si, P.
walkthrough:
**Sort by melting point (y-axis)**

Think about structure first. Si is giant covalent with many strong covalent bonds, so it is highest. P is $\text{P}_4$ simple molecules with weak van der Waals forces, so it is lowest.

Order low to high: $$\text{P} < \text{Mg} < \text{Al} < \text{Si}$$

**Sort by first ionisation energy (x-axis)**

Think about electrons. General increase across Period 3, but Al is lower than Mg because Al removes a 3p electron which is higher in energy and more shielded than Mg 3s electron.

Order low to high: $$\text{Al} < \text{Mg} < \text{Si} < \text{P}$$

**Combine to find the correct plot**

We need Si top and in the middle for x, P bottom right, and Al to the left of Mg on the x-axis with Al just above Mg on the y-axis.

Only one graph has both the y-order $\text{P} < \text{Mg} < \text{Al} < \text{Si}$ and the x-order $\text{Al} < \text{Mg} < \text{Si} < \text{P}$.

options.A: Melting order is nearly right with Si high and P low, but the x-axis is wrong. It shows Mg with lower first ionisation energy than Al. In reality Al is lower than Mg due to the 3p versus 3s electron.
options.B: The x-axis order Al < Mg < Si < P is correct, but the y-axis is wrong. It shows Al with the highest melting point. In reality Si is far highest due to its giant covalent lattice, Al and Mg are in the middle, and P is lowest.
options.C: This is correct on both axes. On the y-axis Si is highest, Al is just above Mg, and P is lowest. On the x-axis Al is lowest, then Mg, then Si, then P is highest, matching the Mg to Al dip.
options.D: This gets Si high correct but fails twice. On the y-axis it shows P higher than Mg, when P should be lowest. On the x-axis it shows Mg lower than Al, when Al should be lower than Mg.
